subject: Hosted API — data residency, retention & deletion (security questionnaire)
messages:
From: Pedro Morales <pedro.morales@altohealth.com>

Cc: security@altohealth.com
Date: 2026-05-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hosted API — residency and retention Qs

Marcus —

Thanks for taking this. Our security team is completing a short vendor questionnaire for the Hosted API. We have a few focused questions on data residency, retention, and deletion so we can confirm Alto Health remains compliant with our internal data residency policy. Can you provide bullet answers we can paste into the questionnaire? Specifically:

- Where are request payloads and generated responses stored geographically for the Hosted API by default? If you replicate for availability, where is the primary copy kept?
- Can customers restrict storage to US-only? If so, how is that guaranteed for hosted customers?
- What are default retention periods for: request/response logs, embeddings, audit logs, and aggregated analytics?
- What is the deletion workflow for a data deletion request (time to delete, endpoints to call, confirmation)?
- Are request bodies used for model training or ML improvements?
- Are logs and stored data encrypted at rest and in transit? Key management details?

We appreciate short, precise answers and any links to SOC2 or architecture diagrams. If better to do a quick call, we can do 30 minutes later today.

—Pedro

Pedro — thanks, Ill put the answers below in short, copy-pasteable bullets for your questionnaire. Ive marked where enterprise (contract) options differ from our default hosted behavior. Referenced evidence attached: SOC2 report and a simplified data flow diagram.

1) Geographic storage (Hosted API default)
- Default: Hosted API customer data (request payloads and generated responses) is stored in the cloud region associated with the customers account. For self-serve accounts created in the US, primary storage resides in a US region (AWS us-west-2 or us-east-1 depending on provisioning).
- Replication: We perform cross-availability-zone replication within the selected region for durability. We do not replicate request/response payloads to other geographic regions by default.
- Enterprise option: We offer a contractual US-only residency guarantee for hosted customers under enterprise terms (we isolate infrastructure and restrict cross-region backups when required).

2) Customer-requested US-only restriction
- Yes — for enterprise customers we can enforce US-only storage by policy and infrastructure configuration. This is enabled during account provisioning and verified via audit logs and architecture controls. For self-serve accounts, the default regional placement is in the region selected at signup; if you require a contractual residency commitment, well need an enterprise agreement to lock region and subprocessors.

3) Default retention periods (Hosted API)
- Request/response logs (full bodies): default retention = 30 days. Stored to support troubleshooting, abuse detection, and billing reconciliation.
- Embeddings and derived artifacts: default retention = 30 days, unless the customer opts into longer-term storage for application use (explicit opt-in at account level).
- Audit logs (control plane events, auth events): default retention = 365 days for operational and security monitoring.
- Aggregated metrics/telemetry: retained for 24 months as aggregated, non-identifiable metrics.
- Note: short-term caches (KV caches used during generation) are ephemeral and not persisted beyond the inference session.

4) Deletion workflow and SLAs
- Deletion request methods: API endpoint for data deletion (DELETE /v1/accounts/{account_id}/data) or support ticket with the account owner identity verification.
- SLA: For standard hosted accounts: deletion confirmation and removal of request/response bodies from primary storage within 72 hours; background propagation and removal from backups within 30 days.
- Enterprise contractual option: expedited deletion and shorter backup retention windows (custom SLAs) can be negotiated.
- Confirmation: We provide a signed deletion confirmation statement and a log entry in the accounts audit trail once deletion is complete.

5) Use of request data for training
- By default, we do NOT use customer request/response payloads for model training or to improve models. Data may be used for platform improvement only in aggregated, de-identified form and only with explicit customer consent. Enterprise customers may have stricter contract language; we can include a no-training clause in the agreement.

6) Encryption and key management
- In transit: TLS 1.2+ for all API traffic.
- At rest: All persistent customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256. Keys are managed via a customer-configurable KMS integration for enterprise customers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). For hosted default accounts, keys are managed by Redwood with automatic rotation; enterprise customers can provide their own KMS keys under an account-level configuration.

7) Subprocessors and data flow
- We use cloud providers (AWS and GCP) as subprocessors for compute and storage. We publish our subprocessors list and maintain Data Processing Agreements (DPAs) with all subprocessors. See attached data-flow diagram for an overview of where data is stored and which services may see decrypted data for operation.

8) Audit evidence and compliance
- Attached: SOC2 Type II report (Redacted) and a simplified data flow diagram. We are open to an encrypted artifact exchange or an NDA first if Alto Health requires.

If you want me to convert the bullets into a one-column answer sheet matching your questionnaire fields, say the word and Ill send it back in that format. Happy to jump on a call if anything needs more detail.

Regards,
Dev Patel
Director, Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

This is excellent, thank you. Two quick follow-ups before I close the questionnaire: 

1) Can you confirm the 72-hour deletion SLA means primary storage is scrubbed within 72 hours and that a signed deletion confirmation will be provided to us?
2) For the "no-training" statement, can Redwood include that clause in the standard enterprise DPA? Alto Health requires it.

If you can send a short set of single-line answers I can paste into our vendor portal it would be helpful. We may also ask for a DocuSign to add the residency clause in the DPA. Otherwise the SOC2 doc and data flow help a lot.

Thanks — well be in touch once we finish the questionnaire.

—Pedro
